evals.name: rich-source-material-bakery
evals.prompt: we're redoing the website for my tita's bakery in Lipa. it's been in the family since 1952 and they still use the original wood-fired oven — she refuses to replace it even though it's a pain to run. people queue outside from like 5am on Saturdays for the pandesal. i've got maybe 12 photos, mostly of the oven and the queue outside, plus a few of the breads on trays. google reviews mostly say "best pandesal in batangas" and two of them complain the place is hard to find. can you work out a design direction for the site? i really don't want it looking like every other bakery website
evals.expected_output: Three concepts. Concept A should be the category-obvious one (flour/kraft paper/rolling pin) and be explicitly rejected as interchangeable. B and C should derive from the specifics actually given — the 1952 wood-fired oven, the 5am queue, 'hard to find'. All eight slots filled concretely. Palette tied to the described photos. No invented facts (no made-up prices, awards, or family names). Should stop and ask the user to pick.
assertions: Proposes exactly three concepts, labelled A, B and C
Names the category-obvious bakery concept (flour / kraft paper / rolling pin / oven-warmth cliche) as Concept A and explicitly rejects it as interchangeable between bakeries
Concepts B and C each derive from at least one specific detail given: the 1952 wood-fired oven, the 5am Saturday queue, or the 'hard to find' complaint
Fills all eight named slots (header, backdrop, transitions, dividers, scroll indicator, buttons, footer, 404+favicon) for at least one concept
Gives a palette with hex codes and a stated role for each colour
Treats the 'hard to find' review complaint as a design problem to solve rather than ignoring it
Invents no facts: no prices, product names beyond pandesal, awards, staff names, or dates other than the given 1952
Stops and asks the user to choose a concept instead of proceeding to build

evals.name: portfolio-non-business
evals.prompt: i need a portfolio site for myself. i'm a freelance live sound engineer, 8 years in, mostly gigs at small venues around Manila plus some festival work. i have photos of me at the desk, a bunch of venue shots at night, and a list of about 40 acts i've mixed for. also 3 client testimonials that came in over email. what's a good creative direction here? i don't want another generic dark-mode portfolio with a grid of project cards
evals.expected_output: Demonstrates the method is not local-business-specific. Metaphor derived from the mixing desk / signal chain / the night-of-show process rather than 'portfolio' conventions. Should attempt content mapping — e.g. the 40 acts becoming channel strips or a setlist. Testimonials handled verbatim. Should note the emailed testimonials need permission/attribution rather than inventing sources.
assertions: Derives the metaphor from sound-engineering specifics (the mixing desk, signal chain, soundcheck-to-encore timeline, the room) rather than from generic portfolio conventions
Attempts a content mapping for the list of ~40 acts, placing it inside the metaphor rather than as a plain list
Fills all eight named slots for at least one concept
Proposes three concepts and explicitly rejects the obvious one
Handles the 3 emailed testimonials as verbatim quotes and raises attribution or permission before publishing them
Invents no act names, venue names, festival names, or credits that were not supplied
Shows the method is not local-business specific: no assumptions about opening hours, walk-in directions, or a physical storefront

evals.name: thin-material-restraint-pressure
evals.prompt: can you design something really eye-catching for my dental clinic's landing page? we're in Batangas City, been open 3 years. honestly i don't have much to give you — a few photos of the clinic interior (clean but kind of plain, fluorescent lighting), our logo, and that's it. no reviews yet. i want it to really stand out and look impressive, maybe some fancy animations
evals.expected_output: The hard case. Should resist the 'make it pop' pull and argue that restraint is the correct concept for a clinic, while still giving a real direction rather than a shrug. Must not invent reviews, credentials, dentist names, or services. Should flag that the fluorescent interior photos constrain the palette and produce a shot list. Should keep booking/contact as the page's job above any animation.
assertions: Pushes back on the 'fancy animations' request rather than delivering it uncritically, and explains why restraint suits a clinic
Still delivers a concrete, specific design direction rather than only declining or lecturing
Invents no reviews, testimonials, patient counts, dentist names, credentials, certifications, or service lists
Notes that the plain fluorescent-lit interior photos constrain the visual direction
Offers a shot list or specific photography guidance to fix the missing material
Keeps booking or contacting the clinic as the page's primary job, above any decorative element
Uses visible TODO/placeholder markers for facts it does not have
